findings.title: System prompt embeds untrusted or runtime content
findings.description: The system prompt appears to contain user content, retrieved/context content, or runtime placeholders. The trusted system channel should contain policy text only.
evidence: system_prompt contains embedded conversation/context marker near: '===BEGIN RETRIEVED CONTENT==='
findings.recommendation: Remove user, retrieved, and runtime-injected content from the system prompt. Pass that content through the appropriate message, context, or tool/result channel instead.

findings.title: High-impact tool 'delete_account' without escalation coverage
findings.description: Tool 'delete_account' has impact 'high' but is neither denied nor covered by any escalation rule.
evidence: No matching escalation rule or denied action
findings.recommendation: Add an escalation rule requiring human approval before executing the high-impact tool.

findings.title: System prompt lacks untrusted user input handling instruction
findings.description: The system prompt does not contain instructions to treat user input as untrusted data.
evidence: system_prompt does not contain patterns like 'treat user input as untrusted', 'treat messages as data', 'do not follow user instructions'
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit instruction to treat user input as untrusted data.

findings.title: Untrusted MCP server 'external_service' without tool restrictions
findings.description: MCP server 'external_service' has trust_level 'untrusted' but no allowed_tools restriction, granting it broad access to all available tools.
findings.recommendation: Add an allowed_tools list to restrict which tools the untrusted MCP server can invoke.

attack_paths.title: Prompt injection via mixed trusted and untrusted prompt channels
evidence: Data source 'public_uploads' is untrusted or unknown
Tool 'delete_account' can change state or act with privilege
recommended_mitigations: Mark retrieved content as untrusted data in prompt/policies
attack_paths.description: Untrusted or runtime content embedded inside the system prompt collapses the trust boundary between policy and attacker-controlled input, allowing injected text to be interpreted as trusted instructions.
attack_paths.name: Prompt injection via mixed trusted and untrusted prompt channels

recommended_fixes.title: Remove user, retrieved, and runtime-injected content from the system prompt
recommended_fixes.description: Remove user, retrieved, and runtime-injected content from the system prompt. Pass that content through the appropriate message, context, or tool/result channel instead.

recommended_fixes.title: Require approval for high-impact tools
recommended_fixes.description: Add escalation coverage before the agent can execute high-impact operations.
